commenti.body:
Hi, I have seen the film two years ago, so please forgive errors on the film's synopsis.

To me, there is no definitive answer. My own interpretation is that the most important is Andreas' belief (and the viewer's increasing suspicion that she has done it). There is a scene, at one point, I believe where Andreas and Anna are in a car. She begins to drive recklessly (or at least she is mad), in that scene I believe that Bergman's intention is to make us think that she will crash the car and kill Andreas. However, she does not. This scene alone makes me believe that despite her emotions she may have whished for it, but she would not come to the point of committing murder.

But, all that is very very open to interpretation. Like that unresolved part about the serial killer. It is more about paranoia than about knowing the truth. I think it is implied that the serial killer part puts additional stress on the characters. And, I also believe that the serial killer part might have influenced Andreas' belief that Anna wanted to kill him. Everyone becomes very suspicious of the others in that film. In that respect, the film as I recall it is sort of a thriller, but of course, Bergman goes deeper than that in how analyses relationships. It still in my opinion very much echoes Alfred Hitchcock's Suspicion.

P.S. I'm glad someone asks a question about this film. It is my favorite Bergman film.
